phase3_findings.description: tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py:70-80 _CatalogCursor.execute picks its answer from parameter shape only; the rule that tests name every relation in kinds is not enforced in code (a missing entry looks like a real 'could not verify a base table' refusal), kinds ignores the schema, and routines / non-zero lower_case_table_names are unused.

tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py:70-80 answers catalog lookups by parameter shape: a two-name routine lookup whose second name is a kinds key gets a TABLE_TYPE back, and a relation missing from kinds gets None; both end in a refusal the test did not intend.

tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:662 and :670-673 say the rows are not read-shaped because the statement does not parse; is_read_shaped only checks the first token (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:167-175).
tests/unit/test_safety.py:1107 unchanged comment about '#' opening a MySQL comment now fits only the sqlite row; the added mysql row ('x\nSHOW ...') has no '#'.

src/sqllens/installers/claude_desktop.py:150-152 derive_default_name docstring says other backends use the database segment, but lines 164-168 strip .db/.sqlite/.sqlite3 for every scheme; untouched by the diff.

tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py:73-80 gives every no-parameter statement (lower_case_table_names,), so SELECT @@SESSION.sql_mode on the remove_sql_modes path would read 0 silently; a two-name routine lookup can be answered as a table-type lookup.
tests/unit/test_cli_claude_desktop.py:184 adds a mysql+pymysql://.../orders.db -> orders case that pins behaviour derive_default_name's docstring contradicts.
tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:670-673 comment names parsing as the reason the rows are not read-shaped; is_read_shaped only checks the first keyword.

tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py relation-lookup branch treats any two-parameter execute whose second parameter is a kinds key as a relation lookup; a mixed-case call can send ('Orders', 'orders') to the routine lookup and get 'BASE TABLE' back as a routine name. Latent; no current test sends such SQL.
